name: PixiTween Director S24: turnaround (the image model draws the product from every side, three.js wears it)
description: The 3D product stops guessing its sides. The image model draws one turnaround sheet from the photo (front, three-quarter, side, back), code cuts the views apart and checks that they agree, Muse checks them against the photo with one redraw at most, and three.js wears them: a 360 degree label strip for round products, a back texture for boxes, pouches and outlines. Any failure falls back to today's single-photo body. Leaves out: an image-to-3D mesh service, characters, an approval gate.

userStories.title: Turnaround prompt
userStories.description: As a drawer of the turnaround (the Muse image model), I want a prompt that asks for one sheet with the same product seen four ways so that the views agree with each other and can be cut apart by code.
steps: Read docs/architecture/turnaround-3d.md, server/art/invent-photo.ts (inventPhotoPrompt and its lint of brand terms) and server/art/lint.ts.
Create server/product3d/turnaround.ts exporting turnaroundPrompt(o: { name?: string; shape: string }): string.

The text asks for exactly one picture of the same product four times in one row, left to right: straight-on front, three-quarter turned 45 degrees, straight-on side turned 90 degrees, straight-on back turned 180 degrees. Same size, same height, same flat soft studio light, a plain white backdrop, clear white space between the four, no text added, no shadows on the floor, no people, no extra objects. Every colour, label and cap detail of the reference photo is kept, and the back shows what the back of such a product carries without inventing new brand names.
Brand and person terms of `name` are taken out with the same lint helpers invent-photo uses.
Create server/product3d/turnaround.test.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: turnaroundPrompt({ shape: 'bottle' }) contains the four angles (front, three-quarter, side, back) and the words 'plain white backdrop'
turnaroundPrompt with a name that holds a brand term from extractBrandTerms does not contain that term
turnaroundPrompt is the same string for the same input

userStories.title: Code checks that the views agree
userStories.description: As a gate before any model look, I want measured checks on the four views so that a sheet whose views are different products is redrawn or dropped without spending a vision call.
steps: Read server/product3d/colour.ts (sideColour, rgbToLab), server/product3d/pixels.ts and the TurnaroundViews type in server/product3d/turnaround.ts.
Create server/product3d/agree.ts exporting viewsAgree(views: TurnaroundViews, photo: Buffer): Promise<{ ok: boolean; problems: string[] }>.

Rules, each a problem sentence when it fails: (1) the front view's mean colour is within Lab distance 18 of the photo's cut-out mean colour; (2) the front view's width over height is within 25 percent of the photo cut-out's; (3) the side view's width is between 0.25 and 1.6 times the front view's width; (4) the back view's mean colour is within Lab distance 28 of the front view's; (5) no view is more than 60 percent transparent pixels inside its own box.

Create server/product3d/agree.test.ts with synthetic views: same-colour views pass; a back view of another hue fails rule 4 with a sentence that names the back view; a front view of another hue than the photo fails rule 1.
acceptanceCriteria: viewsAgree with four views of one colour and a photo of that colour returns ok true and no problems
viewsAgree with a back view of a clearly different hue returns ok false and a problem that mentions 'back'
viewsAgree with a front view of a different hue than the photo returns ok false and a problem that mentions 'front'

userStories.title: Muse checks the sheet against the photo
userStories.description: As a reviewer (Muse, with the photo beside the sheet), I want to say whether the drawn views are the same product as the photo so that a wrong label, cap or colour is redrawn once.
steps: Read server/crew/frame-review.ts (reviewImages use, reviewFrames) and the s23 checkSheets in server/crew/sheet-film/check.ts for the call shape, parsing and ledger use.

In server/product3d/turnaround-check.ts export turnaroundCheckPrompt(o: { name?: string; locks?: string[] }): string, parseTurnaroundCheck(text: string): { ok: boolean; problems: string[] }, and checkTurnaround(ctx, o: { photo: Buffer; sheet: Buffer; name?: string; locks?: string[] }): Promise<{ ok: boolean; problems: string[] }>.

The prompt asks one question: is the product in all four views the product in the first picture (shape, cap, label art, colours), and what is different; reply as JSON { "ok": boolean, "problems": string[] } with at most 4 problems of one sentence each.
parseTurnaroundCheck accepts the JSON inside a code fence or with text around it; anything unreadable returns ok true with no problems (the check never blocks a film).
checkTurnaround calls ctx.meta.spark reviewImages with the photo and the sheet, and adds the cost to ctx.ledger the way checkSheets does.
Create server/product3d/turnaround-check.test.ts with a faked ctx.meta.spark.
acceptanceCriteria: parseTurnaroundCheck of '{"ok":false,"problems":["the back label is blank"]}' returns ok false and that problem
parseTurnaroundCheck of text with no JSON returns ok true and an empty problems list
checkTurnaround makes exactly one reviewImages call and adds one ledger entry

userStories.title: Wrap the views into a 360 degree label strip
userStories.description: As a three.js body for round products, I want a label strip stitched from the front, three-quarter, side and back views so that the bottle shows its true back when it turns.
steps: Read server/product3d/unwrap.ts (findBodyBand, unwrapCylinder, LABEL_WIDTH, LABEL_HEIGHT, how the strip's columns map to angle and where angle 0 sits), server/product3d/unwrap.test.ts and server/product3d/pixels.ts.
Create server/product3d/wrap360.ts exporting wrapStrip(views: TurnaroundViews, side: Rgb): Promise<{ strip: Buffer; band: BodyBand } | undefined>.

For each view find the body band (findBodyBand); undefined when the front view has none. Sample each view's band across its width into angles using x = cx + r * sin(theta), theta from -90 to +90 degrees, so a view covers 180 degrees of the cylinder.

Place the front at angle 0, the three-quarter at 45, the side at 90, the back at 180 (mirror the side view for 270). Between two placed views blend with weights that fall linearly with the angle distance (so a seam is a cross-fade over at most 45 degrees).
Output the same LABEL_WIDTH x LABEL_HEIGHT pixel size and the same angle-to-column mapping as unwrapCylinder so the renderer needs no change.

Create server/product3d/wrap360.test.ts: four flat-coloured cylinders (different colour per view) give a strip whose column at angle 0 is the front colour and at angle 180 the back colour; a front view with no straight body returns undefined.
acceptanceCriteria: the strip column at angle 0 matches the front view's colour and the column at angle 180 matches the back view's colour
the strip has width LABEL_WIDTH and height LABEL_HEIGHT
wrapStrip returns undefined when the front view has no straight body band

userStories.title: prepareProduct3D uses the views
userStories.description: As a product builder, I want prepareProduct3D to take the drawn views so that round products get the 360 strip and flat products get a back texture, and everything else stays as today.
steps: Read server/product3d/prepare.ts and prepare.test.ts, server/product3d/wrap360.ts and the way server/crew/cinematic-cut.ts and server/tools/product3d.ts call prepareProduct3D.
Add `views?: TurnaroundViews` to PrepareInput and `back?: AssetRef` to Prepared3D (additive).
Round shapes with views: texture = wrapStrip(views, side) stored as the 'label' asset; when wrapStrip returns undefined keep today's unwrap.
Flat shapes (box, pouch) and outlines with views: texture stays the front; store the back view (trimmed, same size rules as the front) as a second image asset and return it as `back`.
The cache key gains `:views` when views are given, so the plain and the drawn body never share an entry.
Without `views` the output is identical to today's: existing prepare tests stay unchanged and green. Extend prepare.test.ts with the new cases.
acceptanceCriteria: prepareProduct3D for a bottle with views stores a label strip of LABEL_WIDTH x LABEL_HEIGHT and returns no `back`
prepareProduct3D for a box with views returns a `back` asset and keeps textureKind 'front'

userStories.title: turnaroundFor: draw, cut, check, redraw once, or fall back
userStories.description: As a pipeline step for the product, I want one function that turns a photo into checked views or a plain reason so that a film never fails because of the turnaround.
steps: Read server/product3d/turnaround.ts, agree.ts, turnaround-check.ts, server/crew/cinematic-cut.ts (prepareParts, where the cut-out and the product name are known) and server/env.ts (how flags are read and tested).
Add TURNAROUND to server/env.ts: '0' turns the step off, anything else leaves it on (default on).

Create server/product3d/turnaround-flow.ts exporting turnaroundFor(ctx, o: { photo: Buffer; name?: string; shape: string; locks?: string[]; log: (line: string) => void }): Promise<{ views: TurnaroundViews; sheet: Buffer } | undefined>.

Steps: drawTurnaround; splitTurnaround; viewsAgree; checkTurnaround. If any step fails, redraw once with `extra` set to the problem sentences (one line each) and run the four steps again; a second failure returns undefined and logs 'turnaround: <reason>, using the single-photo body'.

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.
Start only on a branch that already holds the s23 sheet film: confirm server/crew/sheet-film/index.ts exports makeSheetFilm. If it does not, set notes to 'blocked: s23 not merged' and stop.
Run this PRD in its own git worktree (ralph/README.md section 3). Never edit files in the owner's main checkout: its dev server restarts on any server/ edit and kills a film that is building.

`npm test` has 6 known failures outside your files: server/agent/director.test.ts (1), server/http/app.test.ts (1), server/http/middleware.chain.test.ts (2), server/http/handlers/exports.test.ts (1), server/http/handlers/local.test.ts (1). Do not edit those files. The gate passes when no other test fails.
Every Muse call in code goes through ctx.meta.spark (chat or reviewImages) and is added to ctx.ledger like planBoard does. Tests fake ctx.meta.spark; nothing calls the network.

Creative choices stay with Muse (the board, the look, what to revise). Code draws the sheets, measures, checks rules and passes problems back to Muse as words; it never rewrites the board itself except to drop an element Muse named.

Renders in tests are faked: inject the render function (the shape of renderKeyFrames: (composition, times) => Promise<Buffer[]>) and return small sharp-made PNGs. Never launch Chromium in a unit test.

For a browser check never run `npm run dev` and never touch ports 8787, 8797, 5173 or 5199 (the owner's servers). Start your own pair and stop it after: `PORT=8798 DATA_DIR=data-s23 npx tsx server/main.ts` and `DIRECTOR_WEB_PORT=5180 DIRECTOR_API_URL=http://localhost:8798 npx vite --config web/vite.config.ts --port 5180 --strictPort`, then open http://localhost:5180.

debug/ is gitignored: the Clippy example sheets named in readFirst are reachable only if the owner linked debug/storyboard into this worktree. If they are missing, read the design doc's description of them instead; they are for the idea only.
Drawn views are never edited by code (no repainting, no label fixes). A failed view is redrawn by the image model once or the film uses the single-photo body.
Tests never call the image model, a vision model or Chromium: fake ctx.image.edit, ctx.meta.spark and the render function. Test images are made with sharp.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner runs `npm run live -- s24-turnaround --yes` (test server, PORT 8797) with a perfume photo and a can photo; open debug/turnaround/<stamp>/compare.jpg and judge whether the drawn body is better than the single-photo body at 90, 180 and 270 degrees. Expect +30-55 s and about $0.045 per product.
MG-2: owner makes one perfume film in the app: the Plan panel shows the drawn turnaround first in the sheet strip, and the spin shows the drawn back. Set TURNAROUND=0 to compare with the old body.
